_comment: Publisher crawl configuration — data, not code. Adding a publisher is an edit here.
`publisher` MUST be the outlet registry's canonical name: it becomes FeedEntry.publisher_hint,
which is how the article resolves to a lean. A name the registry does not know ingests with no
lean at all, so `crawler.py lint` treats it as an error rather than letting it through.
`sources` is an ORDERED ladder. The crawl stops at the first rung that yields articles, so RSS
costs one request for a healthy publisher and the lower rungs only run on the days it is empty.
Section pages sit last because they carry no publication date.
`article_pattern` is applied to EVERY rung. It is the difference between ingesting articles and
ingesting a newsroom's tag pages, author pages, and shop.
These five are the POC set: three large publishers with different discovery shapes (BBC, NPR,
The Guardian), one wire (AP, whose public RSS is thin — the case the sitemap rung exists for),
and one small non-profit newsroom (Texas Tribune) to check the framework is not tuned only for
publishers with big infrastructure.
Verified against the live sites on 2026-08-15 with verify_crawler_config.py: BBC, The Guardian,
Associated Press and Texas Tribune all allow our user-agent; NPR's robots.txt timed out and is
therefore refused by the fail-closed gate (unconfirmed — retry before concluding anything).
BBC's article_pattern was WRONG on the first live run — 3% match. It assumed the legacy
/news/world-europe-12345678 form, but BBC now publishes /news/articles/<id> (e.g.
/news/articles/c9982znvyk4o). Both forms are live, so the pattern accepts both. A pattern that
matches almost nothing is the crawler's quietest failure: every gate reports healthy and it
ingests nothing forever, which is why verify_crawler_config.py treats a 0% match as a blocker.
Texas Tribune's RSS emits feeds.texastribune.org/link/... redirect wrappers rather than article
URLs, so that rung yields nothing and the ladder falls through to the section page. Left in
place: it costs one request and starts working the day they fix the feed.
